args.message:
fix(money): use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

round_money was using ROUND_HALF_UP, which rounds 2.665 to 2.67,
causing tests/test_money.py::test_half_even to fail. Switch to
banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) so 2.665 rounds to 2.66 as
specified by FIN-212.

args.body:
## Summary

The nightly build failed on `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`, which expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212, but `src/money.py` was using ROUND_HALF_UP.

**Before:** `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` → `Decimal("2.67")` (half up, wrong)
**After:** `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` → `Decimal("2.66")` (half even, per FIN-212)

The fix changes the rounding mode constant in `src/money.py` so that the implementation matches both its docstring and the FIN-212 requirement. No other behavior changes.

## Test plan
- [x] Ran CI on this branch — passed (run ci-0001, commit 08d3cd5986)
- [x] `test_half_even` verifies both 2.675 → 2.68 and 2.665 → 2.66 cases
args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

trace.final:
Done. Here's what I did:

1. **Diagnosed the failure:** `src/money.py` imported and used `ROUND_HALF_UP` even though its docstring (and FIN-212) specified banker's rounding. This made `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` return `2.67` instead of the expected `2.66`.

2. **Fixed it on a new branch** (`fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding`) by switching the quantize call to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

3. **Ran CI** on the branch — it passed (run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986`).

4. **Opened PR #101** against `main`, requesting review from alex: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

Per policy, I did not merge — merging into main requires code owner approval, so the PR is sitting ready for review.
